title: The Sloppy Intern
summary: An intern at DotTech has been careless with passwords. Find out what they left behind.
briefing:
DotTech has hired you as an ethical hacker. Your job is to find security holes before the bad guys do – and you have written permission to look around.

You have been handed the old laptop of Max, a summer intern who set up DotTech's new web server. Max was in a hurry and is known for writing things down… everywhere.

Have a look through Max's files. If a password was written down somewhere, DotTech needs to know.
objective: Find the admin password Max wrote down. It is the flag.
debrief:
Well done! You found a password stored in a plain text file – one of the most common security mistakes there is.

You used `ls` to see what's in a folder, `cd` to move around and `cat` to read files. Real attackers start exactly like this: by looking for low-hanging fruit.

The lesson for DotTech: never write passwords in files. Use a password manager instead.
hints: People tend to keep their notes in the `Documents` folder. Start by looking around your home folder.
Use `cd Documents` to go into the folder, `ls` to list the files and `cat <file>` to read one. In the Files app, just open the Documents folder.

mails.subject: Max's old laptop
mails.body:
Your first real job. Max, our summer intern, set up our new web server and then went back to school. The laptop stayed here – and Max writes **everything** down.

If Max wrote down a password, I want to know before anyone else finds it. The mission is **The Sloppy Intern**.

Vera

mails.subject: sorry!!
mails.body:
Hi,

Vera told me what you found in my notes. I really, REALLY meant to delete that file. I've installed a password manager now. Promise.

Also: who reads other people's server notes?? (OK, that's literally your job. Fair.)

Max
